subject.title: [do not merge] refactor: flip sessions and transcripts to sqlite storage

question: Should OpenClaw ship the one-way SQLite session/transcript cutover and remove the file-shaped Plugin SDK session APIs in the same release?
rationale: The tracker endorses the database-first direction, but this changes persistent private data, downgrade behavior, external plugin contracts, and message continuity; automation cannot choose that permanent compatibility boundary.

options.title: Repair and approve the combined cutover
options.body: Keep the combined migration and API removal, but require a coherent exact-head branch plus inspectable fresh-install and legacy-upgrade proof before merge.

options.title: Stage Plugin SDK removal separately
options.body: Land canonical SQLite storage while preserving or deprecating shipped Plugin SDK surfaces through an explicit transition window.

options.title: Pause the all-at-once migration
options.body: Keep the tracker open and park this branch until the upgrade and API contract can be narrowed into reviewable slices.

recommendation.title: Repair and approve the combined cutover
recommendation.body: Keep the combined migration and API removal, but require a coherent exact-head branch plus inspectable fresh-install and legacy-upgrade proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: Current-main history shows the strongest ownership of the session-store runtime and related state paths.
